summary: @qlik/carbon-core preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, dictionary indirection) and downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, extracts it, chmods 0o755, and invokes the shipped file math_init.js under Bun on npm install. Even when Bun is already present, setup.mjs still executes math_init.js under Bun. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle (string-array shuffling via WV8StW, >700-element lookup table, encoded identifiers) that is never imported by src/index.js and is unrelated to the package's stated React Native rendering purpose. Executing the payload under an alternate runtime bypasses scanners that only trace Node-resolvable code. The package presents Qlik branding (name @qlik/carbon-core, author Qlik, repository qlik-trial/carbon-core) while shipping this dropper, consistent with either a namespace impersonation of the @qlik scope or compromise of a legitimate Qlik package.
